posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
Reveal the Flaws is one of the most talked about cards since Vengeance went live. The silver being with the Alchemy symbol on its head is being talked about a lot. Is it the Cosmic Entity? A servant to said entity? Is it connected with the Scholar or the Hermetic?

Matriarch. We have *never* seen card art to date that has a villain attacking a villain. What does that tell us? Will she end up being a hero? She has speaking text in the Final Wasteland environment that didnt sound very evil. Captain Cosmic seems to be rushing to her rescue! Wait, Captain Cosmic is rushing to the Matriarch?

Look at the flavor text. "There! Run to the Center! Its now or never!"

"The Child is the center" - time crazed prisoner

"I rule from the center to the sea" - Matriarchs Mask

Common now. There is something here.

posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
I've found it in other places (such as tourism guides), but the phrase "From the center to the sea" could refer to a poem (seen here).  The Shan Van Vocht (translation: The Poor Old Woman) describes the Irish rebellion of 1798.

Her name (Lillian Merle Corvus) is largely of latin derivation, but that doesn't rule out an Irish angle. Lily (her nickname, and what Lillian means) is an important flower in Irish culture (though in fairness, its important in a lot of cultures).

This brings me to the Morrigan.  

she is associated with a LOT of stuff- some good, some bad.  Things like war and death, but also fertility, creativity, and poetry. she's associated with druids, bards, and circles.  She's often associated with crows, or depicted as one.

If she does become a hero, I could see her taking the Morrigan name.   

 

Onto reveal the flaws

In Reveal the Flaws, the Matriarch is being held by the silver creature.  Her eyes are glowing purple- as are its eyes.  Prisoner?  controller?  both being held in the grip of a larger force acting through the mask?

It could well be that she kept seeking more and more power, and something is now using her...

posts.name: LACK OF SUBTLETY
posts.cooked:
The way I have always viewed the Reveal the Flaws image is that, in the midst of a battle with the Matriarch, Progeny erupted and started attacking everyone there. 

 

The turn-to good-guy for The Matriarch would come when the heroes risked themselves to save her from Progeny. I do think it's a little odd that she ends up with the Dark Watch when none of them are present in the scene, but maybe she just decided she wanted to help out her home town and started working with the heroes who were there. Or, if Nightmist went missing around the same time, she saw that they needed her help.
